note: PLACEHOLDER. Every params object here validates against the published race_opponent_actions manifest input_schema (additionalProperties: false, $refs inlined the way publish_experiments.py inlines them), and every value is plausible, but nobody has dispatched one. So a verdict drawn from this list is a claim about the pipeline, not about the agent. EIGHT cases, and DEFAULT_JUDGE_CONFIG.gates.minCases is 20. A corpus verdict over this list therefore resolves CAN'T SAY however the judge voted, because the floor was set from measured agent non-determinism and eight runs measure that rather than the branch. Eight is deliberate and not a rounding error: one clean baseline plus seven single-axis variations is what one change can author honestly across nine agents. Whether to grow every list to 20 or to lower the floor is still open — do not read the shortfall as a decision. Varied along: whether the district trio is present, which is the branch that decides whether a card carries a constituent number or goes out numberless with haystaq_status no_district — the schema's dependencies clause makes state, l2_district_type and l2_district_name all-or-nothing, so cases carry all three or none; the threat-tier mix, since tiers drive card ordering and a list that is all low_priority should not read like a primary threat; how much of each persisted summary survived, including an opponent whose overview, background and issues are all null; field size, one to three opponents; and how much candidate platform there is to draw the candidate side of a contrast from, full, bio-only, or absent, since absent or thin means fewer cards rather than invented ones. People are fictional placeholders in the house style (gp-webapp e2e-tests briefings.spec.ts uses 'Test Official'); this file is public, so no real person is named. States, cities, office titles and L2 voter file column names are real.

opponents.overview_text: Four-year incumbent on the Minneapolis City Council for Ward 3, previously a regional transportation planner. Runs on continuity: the inclusionary zoning update, the pedestrian safety plan, and holding the levy. Endorsed by the building trades and two neighborhood associations, which is the strongest organized backing in the ward.
opponents.background_text: B.A. in urban studies; eight years at a council of governments doing corridor studies before first election in 2022. No prior elected office. Term ends January 2027.
issues_that_matter: Supports the inclusionary zoning update but has not said whether the density bonus loophole stays in.
Funds the pedestrian safety plan at the level the plan asks for.
Holds the property tax levy flat while protecting library hours.

opponents.overview_text: First-time candidate, eleven years running a hardware store on the avenue. Runs on process complaints rather than policy: permit turnaround, published police response-time targets, and no new commercial street assessments without an owner vote.
opponents.background_text: No prior public office. Small business owner.
issues_that_matter: Wants a ten-business-day permit guarantee.
Wants published police response-time targets by neighborhood.

candidate_platform.bio: I taught eighth-grade science in this city for twelve years and chaired my neighborhood association land-use committee for four. I am running because the people who are priced out of this ward never get asked what would have kept them here.

issues.title: Housing affordability
issues.description: Rent stabilization on buildings over twenty units, and no density bonus that does not produce units at sixty percent of area median income.

issues.title: Transit reliability
issues.description: Restore fifteen-minute headways on the two busiest bus lines before any new capital project is funded.
